WaterTable.title: Water Table

TemperatureAtDepth.title: Temperature At Depth

C1.title: C1
C1.description:
First coefficient for adjusting the Pedersen viscosity model.

In Pedersen 1984, the mixture molecular weight is given by MWmix = c1 x (MWw ^ c2 - MWn ^ c2) + MWn. Values provided by the original publication for c1 and c2 are 0.291, and 1.0 respectively.

In Pedersen 1987, the mixture molecular weight is given by MWmix = c1 x (MWw ^ c2 - MWn ^ c2) + MWn. Values provided by the original publication for c1 and c2 are 1.304 x 10^-4, and 2.303 respectively.

C2.title: C2
C2.description:
Second coefficient for adjusting the Pedersen viscosity model.

In Pedersen 1984, the mixture molecular weight is given by MWmix = c1 x (MWw ^ c2 - MWn ^ c2) + MWn. Values provided by the original publication for c1 and c2 are 0.291, and 1.0 respectively.

In Pedersen 1987, the mixture molecular weight is given by MWmix = c1 x (MWw ^ c2 - MWn ^ c2) + MWn. Values provided by the original publication for c1 and c2 are 1.304 x 10^-4, and 2.303 respectively.

C3.title: C3
C3.description:
Third coefficient for adjusting the Pedersen viscosity model.

In Pedersen 1984, the mixture rotational coupling coefficient is found by αmix = 1 + c3*ρrm^c4 + MWmix^c5. Values provided by the original publication for c3, c4, and c5 are 7.747 x 10^-5, 4.265, and 0.8579 respectively.

In Pedersen 1987, the mixture rotational coupling coefficient is found by αmix = 1 + c3*ρrm^c4 + MWmix^c5. Values provided by the original publication for c3, c4, and c5 are 7.378 x 10^-3, 1.847, and 0.5173 respectively.

C4.title: C4
C4.description:
Fourth coefficient for adjusting the Pedersen viscosity model.

In Pedersen 1984, the mixture rotational coupling coefficient is found by αmix = 1 + c3*ρrm^c4 + MWmix^c5. Values provided by the original publication for c3, c4, and c5 are 7.747 x 10^-5, 4.265, and 0.8579 respectively.

In Pedersen 1987, the mixture rotational coupling coefficient is found by αmix = 1 + c3*ρrm^c4 + MWmix^c5. Values provided by the original publication for c3, c4, and c5 are 7.378 x 10^-3, 1.847, and 0.5173 respectively.

C5.title: C5
C5.description:
Fifth coefficient for adjusting the Pedersen viscosity model.

In Pedersen 1984, the mixture rotational coupling coefficient is found by αmix = 1 + c3*ρrm^c4 + MWmix^c5. Values provided by the original publication for c3, c4, and c5 are 7.747 x 10^-5, 4.265, and 0.8579 respectively.

In Pedersen 1987, the mixture rotational coupling coefficient is found by αmix = 1 + c3*ρrm^c4 + MWmix^c5. Values provided by the original publication for c3, c4, and c5 are 7.378 x 10^-3, 1.847, and 0.5173 respectively.

C6.title: C6
C6.description:
Sixth coefficient for adjusting the Pedersen viscosity model.

In Pedersen 1984, the reference rotational coupling coefficient is found by α0 = 1 + c6*ρrm^c4. A typical default value of c6 is c3 x MWo^c5, or 8.377x 10^-4.

In Pedersen 1987, the reference rotational coupling coefficient is found by α0 = 1 + c6*ρrm^c4. A typical default value of c6 is c3 x MWo^c5, or 0.031.

To capture when Measurement have been made at Standard Conditions (25°C / 100 kPa)
Mutually Exclusive with Pressure/Temperature.
Capture

NonStandardConditionsReference.title: Non Standard Conditions Reference
NonStandardConditionsReference.description: Open Text Box to capture the P & T Reference when measurements are made at non standard conditions (such as "Reservoir", "Tank",…)

SequencedComponentList.title: Sequenced Component List
SequencedComponentList.description: Array of components used in defining the rows and columns of this binary interaction coefficient matrix. The order of the components should be maintained when defining the associated values, e.g., [a,b,c,d,e,. . .].

Elements.title: Elements
Elements.description: Array of length n(n-1)/2, where n is equal to the number of components in SequencedComponentList, comprising the lower triangle of kij values within the binary interaction coefficient matrix in (row,column) order, e.g., [kij value for (2,1), kij value for (3,1), kij value for (3,2), kij value for (4,1), kij value for (4,2), kij value for (4,3), value for (5,1), etc.].  Note the array does not include the values of the diagonal, i.e. where the row and column component are the same.

MolecularWeight.title: Molecular Weight
MolecularWeight.description: Array of molecular weights corresponding to SequencedComponentList values.

CarbonContent.title: Carbon Content
CarbonContent.description: Array of the carbon mole to component mole ratio values corresponding to SequencedComponentList values.

CriticalTemperature.title: Critical Temperature
CriticalTemperature.description: Array of critical temperature values corresponding to SequencedComponentList values.

CriticalPressure.title: Critical Pressure
CriticalPressure.description: Array of critical pressure values corresponding to SequencedComponentList values.

CriticalVolume.title: Critical Volume
CriticalVolume.description: Array of critical volume (VCrit) values corresponding to SequencedComponentList values.

CriticalCompressibilityFactor.title: Critical Compressibility Factor
CriticalCompressibilityFactor.description: Array of critical compressibility factor values corresponding to SequencedComponentList values. It could also be calculated from critical temperature, pressure and volume values.

AcentricFactor.title: Acentric Factor
AcentricFactor.description: Array of acentric factor values corresponding to SequencedComponentList values.

Parachor.title: Parachor
Parachor.description: Array of parachor values corresponding to SequencedComponentList values.

SpecificGravity.title: Specific Gravity
SpecificGravity.description: Array of specific gravity values corresponding to SequencedComponentList values.

NormalBoilingPoint.title: Normal Boiling Point
NormalBoilingPoint.description: Array of normal boiling point values corresponding to SequencedComponentList values.

NonDimensionalVolumeShift.title: Non-Dimensional Volume Shift
NonDimensionalVolumeShift.description:
Non-dimensional volume shift parameters used in the Peneloux et. al. volume correction within the cubic equation of state. For its usage, the component's molar volume accounting for the peneloux volume shift is equal to the component's molar volume without the peneloux volume shift MINUS the NonDimensionalVolumeShift times the b parameter.
A typical non-dimenional volume shift for Methane is near 0.02 for SRK and -0.19 for PR (Peng Robinson). A typical non-dimensional volume shift for n-heptane is near 0.15 for SRK and 0.02 for PR.

DimensionalVolumeShift.title: Dimensional Volume Shift
DimensionalVolumeShift.description: Dimensional volume shift parameters used in the Peneloux et. al. volume correction within the cubic equation of state. For its usage, the component's molar volume accounting for the peneloux volume shift is equal to the component's molar volume without the peneloux volume shift MINUS the DimensionalVolumeShift.

FormulationMethodID.title: Formulation Method ID
FormulationMethodID.description: Identifies the formulation method used in generating the numerical values assigned to the model property (e.g., Peng-Robinson).  There is only one FormulationMethodID identified for an equation of state within a compositional model.

LiFactor.title: Li Factor
LiFactor.description: A multiplication factor to correct the critical temperature calculated by algorithms within some simulator applications. There is only one Li Factor identified for an equation of state within a compositional model.

SurfaceDensity.title: Surface Density
SurfaceDensity.description: The surface mass density of water.

ReferencePressure.title: Reference Pressure
ReferencePressure.description: This a pressure reference (e.g., Initial reservoir pressure) used in defining the water properties of the black oil fluid model.

FormationVolumeFactor.title: Formation Volume Factor
FormationVolumeFactor.description: This is the water formation volume factor values corresponding to the reference pressure.

Viscosity.title: Viscosity
Viscosity.description: This is the water viscosity corresponding to the reference pressure.

Compressibility.title: Compressibility
Compressibility.description: This is the average water compressibility corresponding to the reference pressure and used in calculating the formation volume factor at other pressures.

ViscosityCompressibility.title: Viscosity Compressibility
ViscosityCompressibility.description: This is the average water viscosity compressibility corresponding to the reference pressure andf used in calculating the viscosity at other pressures.

Pressure.title: Pressure
Pressure.description: This a pressure reference (e.g Initial reservoir pressure) used in defining the water properties of the black oil fluid model.

FormationVolumeFactor.title: Formation Volume Factor
FormationVolumeFactor.description: This is the water formation volume factor values corresponding to the reference pressure.

Viscosity.title: Viscosity
Viscosity.description: This is the water viscosity corresponding to the reference pressure.

TrueVerticalDepths.title: True Vertical Depths
TrueVerticalDepths.description: Array of True Vertical Depth (TVD) Values to be used as a reference for any other property mapped against depth. This column is required if any other property is populated.

Temperatures.title: Temperatures
Temperatures.description: Array of Temperature Values at a given Depth. The usage of Temperature against Depth is mutually exclusive with the usage of any other property.

CompositionTypeID.title: Composition Type ID
CompositionTypeID.description: Indicating that the table consists of phase component mole fractions versus depth. (Total, Liquid, Vapor, Aqueous, Residual Oil, Solid)

TrueVerticalDepth.title: True Vertical Depth
TrueVerticalDepth.description: A depth (TVD) value at which the component mole fractions will be specified.

ComponentMoleFractions.title: Component Mole Fractions
ComponentMoleFractions.description: A list of component mole fractions at the designated depth corresponding to the appropriate component id (e.g. 0.0121, 0.0194, etc.). These values should sum up to one.

PhaseTypeID.title: Phase Type ID
PhaseTypeID.description: Indicating that the table consists of phase component mole fractions versus depth. (Total, Liquid, Vapor, Aqueous, Residual Oil, Solid)

MolePercent.title: Mole Percent
MolePercent.description: The molar percentage of this phase.

MassPercent.title: Mass Percent
MassPercent.description: The volume percentage of this phase.

VolumePercent.title: Volume Percent
VolumePercent.description: The volume percentage of this phase.

Density.title: Density
Density.description: The mass density of this phase.

MoleVolume.title: Mole Volume
MoleVolume.description: The mole volume of this phase.

MoleWeight.title: Mole Weight
MoleWeight.description: The molecular weight of this phase.

ZFactor.title: Z Factor
ZFactor.description: The Z factor of this phase.

ComponentMoleFractions.title: Component Mole Fractions
ComponentMoleFractions.description: A list of component mole fractions corresponding to the SequencedComponentList (e.g. 0.0121, 0.0194, etc.). These values should sum up to one.

ComponentFugacities.title: Component Fugacities
ComponentFugacities.description: A list of calculated component fugacities corresponding to the SequencedComponentList. Fugacity is defined as the pressure an ideal gas would require to have the same chemical potential as a real gas at a given temperature.

PhaseIndex1.title: Phase Index 1
PhaseIndex1.description: Identifies the first PhaseIndex value within PhaseProperties that is used for this InterfacialTension calculation.

PhaseIndex2.title: Phase Index 2
PhaseIndex2.description: Interfacial Tension value for the interface of the phases identified by PhaseIndex1 and PhaseIndex2.

Value.title: Value
Value.description: Interfacial Tension value for the interface of the phases identified by PhaseIndex1 and PhaseIndex2.

Pressure.title: Pressure
Pressure.description: Defines the pressure used in this flash validation example.

Temperature.title: Temperature
Temperature.description: Defines the temperature used in this flash validation example.

PhaseProperties.title: Phase Properties
PhaseProperties.description: Properties, such as relative amount, composition, density, viscosity, and z factor, for phases identified in this FlashValidationExample.  Each unique phase is identified by both its CompositionTypeID and its PhaseIndex.

InterfacialTensions.title: Interfacial Tensions
InterfacialTensions.description: Interfacial tensions between pairs of phases in this FlashValidationExample.  Each element specifies PhaseIndex1 and PhaseIndex2, the two PhaseIndex values within PhaseProperties that were used for each interfacial tension value.
